title: Microsoft Purview Compliance Manager: assess Azure, AWS and Google Cloud through Microsoft Defender for Cloud
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, configuration paths, permissions and licensing statements are supported. It distinguishes the documented integration from the government's still-uncertain rollout and correctly warns that the automatic-testing setting does not control Defender for Cloud actions.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes a Compliance Manager integration with Defender for Cloud for Microsoft 365, Azure, GCP and AWS, with resource-level testing and cloud-specific guidance.
claims.quote: Compliance Manager now integrates with Microsoft Defender for Cloud, allowing customers to assess their compliance posture across Microsoft 365, Azure, Google Cloud Platform, and Amazon Web Services with resource-level testing and cloud-specific guidance.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; licensing.notes; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The integration requires at least one Microsoft Azure subscription.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Scope; licensing.notes; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Defender for Cloud must be enabled for Compliance Manager to receive cloud-monitoring signals.
claims.quote: and then enable Defender for Cloud so that Compliance Manager can receive the necessary signals to monitor your cloud services.

claims.claim: Setup includes assigning at least one supported standard to the subscription.
claims.quote: Assign at least one of the supported standards listed below to your subscription by selecting Enable on the standard's row.

claims.claim: Assessment creation includes selecting a supported regulation.
claims.quote: When you create an assessment in Compliance Manager, you'll select a supported regulation

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Assessment creation includes choosing one or more services to assess.
claims.quote: and then choose one or more services to assess.

claims.claim: Compliance Manager automatically monitors configurations in the selected services to evaluate controls.
claims.quote: Compliance Manger then provides automatic monitoring of configurations in your selected services to determine whether controls are passing or failing.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: Defender for Cloud signals automatically determine testing results for technical improvement actions implemented through the integration.
claims.quote: If the testing source is Defender for Cloud, then the action pertains to cloud services such as Microsoft Azure, Amazon Web Services (AWS), and Google Cloud Platform (GCP) ... Technical actions are automatically tested and monitored.

claims.claim: A non-Microsoft service outside the supported cloud-service list can be added as a new service when creating an assessment.
claims.quote: If you want to assess a non-Microsoft service that isn't listed above, you can add it as a new service when you're creating a new assessment.

claims.claim: Adding such a new service uses the universal version of the regulation.
claims.quote: When you add a new service, the universal version of the underlying regulation is used

claims.claim: Implementation and testing for the added new service are manual.
claims.quote: and you perform manual implementation and testing work.

claims.claim: Assessments can select service subscriptions in scope for Defender for Cloud and pull their matching-regulation automated test results.
claims.quote: If you choose subscriptions that are in scope within Defender for Cloud for a matching regulation, automated test results are pulled from Defender for Cloud and shown in the assessment.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Adding a standard to Defender for Cloud's compliance dashboard automatically surfaces its resource-level compliance data in Compliance Manager, including AWS and GCP standards.
claims.quote: When you add any standard to your compliance dashboard (including compliance standards monitoring other clouds like AWS and GCP), the resource-level compliance data is automatically surfaced in Compliance Manager for the same standard.

claims.claim: Defender for Cloud calls these standards and Compliance Manager calls them regulations.
claims.quote: Defender for Cloud refers to “standards,” while Compliance Manager uses “regulations” to refer to the same thing.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Compliance Manager testing-source setting cannot change testing source for actions on services supported by Defender for Cloud.
claims.quote: Testing source can't be changed on actions for services supported by Defender for Cloud.

claims.claim: Testing logic and scope for a disputed automated result can instead be altered in the related Defender for Cloud assessment.
claims.quote: If you don't agree with an automated testing result, you can go to the related assessment in Defender for Cloud to alter the testing logic and scope.

claims.claim: Compliance Manager access requires at least Compliance Manager Reader or Microsoft Entra Global Reader.
claims.quote: Users need at least the Compliance Manager reader role, or Microsoft Entra global reader role, to access Compliance Manager.

claims.claim: Connecting an AWS account requires admin permissions in that account.
claims.quote: Connecting to the accounts requires admin permissions in the AWS or GCP accounts being used

claims.claim: Connecting a GCP account requires admin permissions in that account.
claims.quote: Connecting to the accounts requires admin permissions in the AWS or GCP accounts being used

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Connecting AWS or GCP accounts involves configuration inside those services.
claims.quote: and some configuration steps within AWS or GCP. These steps are detailed in the wizard.

claims.claim: GCC High and DoD customers can set Compliance Manager user permissions and roles only in Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: Customers in US Government Community (GCC) High and Department of Defense (DoD) environments can only set user permissions and roles for Compliance Manager in Microsoft Entra ID.

claims.claim: Non-technical actions implemented through Defender for Cloud must be manually tested.
claims.quote: Whether they can be automatically tested or not depends on the action type: ... Non-technical actions must be manually tested.

claims.claim: Manual-action statuses do not synchronise between Compliance Manager and Defender for Cloud.
claims.quote: Manual actions don't synchronize status between Compliance Manager and Defender for Cloud. You can update the status in either location, however the statuses won't synch.

claims.claim: An improvement action's score aggregates subscription scores, so a failing subscription contributes to the action's aggregate.
claims.quote: The overall score you receive for the improvement action is an aggregate of the individual scores of each subscription within that service.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: A separate charge or meter specific to this integration is not published in the checked Microsoft documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: "Compliance Manager" "Defender for Cloud" integration pricing license additional charge meter; integration price and pricing queries. Read multicloud, cloud-settings, setup, CSPM pricing and Purview service-description excerpt; no integration-specific meter found.

claims.claim: The mixed licensing model reflects Compliance Manager licensing plus Defender for Cloud plan requirements and potential resource-based charges.
claims.quote: Organizations must have at least one subscription within Microsoft Azure and then enable Defender for Cloud ... If you don't see the dashboard above and instead see a notice about insufficient licensing, follow the prompts to activate an applicable Defender for Cloud plan.

claims.claim: After connecting AWS or GCP accounts, administrators can begin assigning standards within about an hour.
claims.quote: When you complete this process, you can begin assigning standards to your connected AWS or GCP subscriptions within about an hour

claims.claim: Full data from connected AWS or GCP accounts can take up to 24 hours to appear.
claims.quote: though full data can take up to 24 hours to appear.

claims.claim: Compliance Manager Administrator or Global Administrator is required to access Compliance Manager settings and change automated testing.
claims.quote: The Compliance Manager Administrator and the Global Administrator for your organization can change the settings for automated testing at any time.

claims.claim: Adding a regulatory compliance standard requires Owner or Policy Contributor.
claims.quote: You need Owner or Policy Contributor permissions to add a standard.

claims.claim: The Microsoft Purview portal path is Settings > Compliance Manager > Testing source > Turn off automatic testing for all actions.
claims.quote: select the Settings icon at the top of the page, then select Compliance Manager. ... Select Testing source from the left navigation. ... Turn off automatic testing for all actions.

claims.claim: A documented automation operation for the Compliance Manager automatic-testing setting was not found.
claims.quote: Searched: Compliance Manager automatic testing Testing source PowerShell API; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell "ComplianceManager" "testing"; Security & Compliance PowerShell Compliance Manager automatic testing. Read setup, improvement-actions and SCC PowerShell overview.

claims.claim: The automatic-testing setting is an organisation-wide Compliance Manager setting, with an all-actions option and individual-action selection.
claims.quote: The Compliance Manager Administrator and the Global Administrator for your organization can change the settings for automated testing at any time. ... You can turn off automated testing for common improvement actions, or turn it on for individual actions.

claims.claim: Changes to the automated-testing setting are reflected in the audit log.
claims.quote: When you change a setting, it will be reflected in the audit log.

claims.claim: The cloud-settings page gives Defender for Cloud > Environment settings > subscription > Edit settings > Policy settings > Security policy > Industry & regulatory standards > standard > Enable.
claims.quote: select Environment settings ... Find the subscription ... select Edit settings. ... under Policy settings, select Security policy. ... under Industry & regulatory standards. ... selecting Enable on the standard's row.

claims.claim: The alternative Azure portal route is Microsoft Defender for Cloud > Regulatory compliance > Manage compliance policies > account > Security policies > standard > On.
claims.quote: Navigate to Microsoft Defender for Cloud > Regulatory compliance. ... Select Manage compliance policies. ... Select an account or management account ... Select Security policies. ... Locate the standard you want to enable and toggle the status to On.

claims.claim: Standards used by the integration are assigned in Defender for Cloud rather than through Compliance Manager.
claims.quote: Once you have Defender for Cloud, you need to assign the relevant industry and regulatory standards to your subscriptions.

claims.claim: The checked Learn documentation does not describe an end-user-facing change from this integration.
claims.quote: Searched: "Compliance Manager" "Defender for Cloud" "end users". Read multicloud, cloud-settings, setup and improvement-actions; these describe assessment creation, testing, permissions and setup, not an end-user-facing change.

claims.claim: The variable cost rating reflects the resource-based Defender CSPM billing described in the briefing.
claims.quote: Defender CSPM billing is based on specific resources enabled in your subscriptions or connectors.
